summary: A shomer who was not paid lost the animal or things he was watching. If he paid the owner instead of swearing, he gets the thief's extra payments; if he swore instead, the owner gets them.

chunks.he: הַמַּפְקִיד אֵצֶל חֲבֵרוֹ בְּהֵמָה אוֹ כֵלִים,
chunks.en: If someone left an animal or vessels with his friend to watch,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits an animal or vessels with another, who is acting as an unpaid bailee,

chunks.en: and they were stolen or lost,
chunks.st: and they were stolen or they were lost, and

chunks.en: and the watchman paid and did not want to swear,
chunks.st: the bailee paid the owner the value of the deposit, and did not wish to take an oath
chunks.stMore: that he did not misappropriate the item and that he was not negligent in safeguarding it, that will effect who keeps the deposit if it is found or returned.

chunks.he: שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם נִשְׁבָּע וְיוֹצֵא,
chunks.en: even though the Sages said a free watchman swears and goes free,
chunks.explain: He swears he did not take it and was not careless.
chunks.st: The bailee may also choose to take the oath, as the Sages said: An unpaid bailee takes an oath, and he is thereby released from the liability to pay the owner.

chunks.en: if the thief is found,
chunks.st: If the thief is later found,

chunks.en: he pays double.
chunks.explain: A thief must pay back twice what he stole.
chunks.st: the thief pays the double payment.

chunks.en: If he slaughtered or sold it,
chunks.st: If the deposited item was a sheep or an ox and the thief slaughtered or sold it,

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.explain: Four times for a sheep, five times for an ox.
chunks.st: he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: To whom does he pay?
chunks.st: To whom does the thief pay?

chunks.en: To the one who had the deposit with him.
chunks.explain: The watchman paid, so he now owns it.
chunks.st: He gives the payment to the one who had the deposit in his
chunks.stMore: possession when it was stolen, i.e., the bailee. When the bailee paid the owner for the stolen item, the owner granted the rights to the item to the bailee. Therefore, the bailee is entitled to any payment the thief presents for the item, be it compensation for the item’s value or a fine.

chunks.en: If the watchman swore and did not want to pay,
chunks.st: In the case of a bailee who took an oath and did not wish to pay,

chunks.en: if the thief is found,
chunks.st: if the thief is then found

chunks.en: he pays double.
chunks.st: and required to pay the double payment,

chunks.en: If he slaughtered or sold it,
chunks.st: or if he slaughtered or sold the animal

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.st: and is required to pay the fourfold or fivefold payment,

chunks.en: To whom does he pay?
chunks.st: to whom does the thief pay?

chunks.en: To the owner of the deposit.
chunks.st: He gives the payment to the owner of the deposit, not the bailee.

summary: Someone rented a cow and lent it to another person, and it died a normal death. The Tanna Kamma says the renter swears and the borrower pays him; Rabbi Yosei says the money goes back to the cow's owner.

chunks.en: If someone rents a cow from his friend and lends it to another person,
chunks.st: In the case of one who rents a cow from another, and this renter then lends it to another person,

chunks.en: and it died the normal way,
chunks.st: and the cow dies in its typical manner, i.e., of natural causes, in the possession of the borrower,

chunks.en: the renter swears that it died the normal way,
chunks.explain: A renter does not pay when an animal dies by itself.
chunks.st: the renter takes an oath to the owner of the cow that the cow died in its typical manner,

chunks.en: and the borrower pays the renter.
chunks.explain: A borrower pays even when it dies by itself.
chunks.st: and the borrower pays the renter
chunks.stMore: for the cow that he borrowed. A renter is exempt in a case of damage due to circumstances beyond his control, including death, but a borrower is liable to compensate the owner even for damage due to circumstances beyond his control.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: How can that one do business
chunks.st: How does the other party, i.e., the renter, do business with

chunks.en: with his friend's cow?
chunks.st: and profit from another’s cow?

chunks.en: Rather, the cow's value goes back to its owner.
chunks.st: Rather, the value of the cow should be returned to the owner.
chunks.stMore: The renter need not take an oath, but the borrower must compensate the owner of the cow.

summary: A man says he took money from one of two people, or was given money by one of their fathers, but does not know which one. He must pay each of them the full amount.

chunks.en: If he said to two people,
chunks.st: If one said to two people:

chunks.en: "I stole 100 zuz from one of you,
chunks.st: I robbed one of you of one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and I do not know which of you,"
chunks.st: but I do not know from which of you I took the money,

chunks.en: or, "The father of one of you
chunks.st: or if one said to two people: The father of one of you

chunks.en: left 100 zuz with me,
chunks.st: deposited one hundred dinars with me,

chunks.en: and I do not know which one he is,"
chunks.st: but I do not know the father of which of you he is,

chunks.en: he gives 100 zuz to this one and 100 zuz to that one,
chunks.st: then he gives one hundred dinars to this person and one hundred dinars to that person.

chunks.en: because he admitted it by himself.
chunks.st: This is because there is no way to determine which of them is entitled to the money, and he admitted his obligation at his own initiative.

summary: Two people left money with one person; each says the bigger amount was his. The Tanna Kamma gives each the smaller amount and puts the rest away until Eliyahu comes; Rabbi Yosei says to put it all away so the cheater loses.

chunks.en: Two people left money with one person,
chunks.st: In the case of two people who deposited money with one person,

chunks.en: this one 100 zuz and that one 200,
chunks.st: and this one deposited one hundred dinars and that one deposited two hundred dinars, and when they come to collect their deposit,

chunks.en: this one says, "Mine was 200,"
chunks.st: this one says: My deposit was two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and that one says, "Mine was 200."
chunks.st: and that one says: My deposit was two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: He gives 100 zuz to this one and 100 zuz to that one,
chunks.st: the bailee gives one hundred dinars to this one and one hundred dinars to that one.

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁאָר יְהֵא מֻנָּח עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
chunks.en: and the rest stays put until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: And the rest of the money, i.e., the contested one hundred dinars, will be placed in a safe place until Elijah comes and prophetically determines the truth.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: If so, what did the cheater lose?
chunks.st: If so, what did the swindler lose?
chunks.stMore: He lost nothing by claiming the one hundred dinars that belongs to another, and he has no incentive to admit the truth.

chunks.en: Rather, all of it stays put
chunks.st: Rather, the entire deposit will be placed in a safe place

chunks.en: until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.explain: Then the cheater may admit the truth.
chunks.st: until Elijah comes. As
chunks.stMore: his fraud will cause him to lose even the one hundred dinars that he deposited, perhaps he will be discouraged from making a fraudulent claim.

summary: Two people left two vessels, a cheap one and an expensive one, and each says the expensive one is his. Each gets the cheap one's value and the rest waits for Eliyahu; Rabbi Yosei says to put it all away.

chunks.en: And the same with two vessels,
chunks.st: And likewise, if two people deposited two vessels,

chunks.en: one worth 100 zuz
chunks.st: one worth one hundred dinars

chunks.en: and one worth 1,000 zuz.
chunks.st: and one worth one thousand dinars,

chunks.en: This one says, "The nice one is mine,"
chunks.st: and this one says: The expensive vessel is mine,

chunks.en: and that one says, "The nice one is mine."
chunks.st: and that one says: The expensive vessel is mine,

chunks.en: He gives the small one to one of them,
chunks.st: the bailee gives the small vessel to one of them,

chunks.he: וּמִתּוֹךְ הַגָּדוֹל נוֹתֵן דְּמֵי קָטָן לַשֵּׁנִי,
chunks.en: and from the big one he gives the small one's value to the other,
chunks.explain: He sells the big one to get the money.
chunks.st: and from the proceeds of the sale of the large vessel he gives the value of the small vessel to the other,

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁאָר יְהֵא מֻנָּח עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
chunks.en: and the rest stays put until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: and the rest of the money is placed in a safe place until Elijah comes.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: If so, what did the cheater lose?
chunks.st: If so, what did the swindler lose?

chunks.en: Rather, all of it stays put
chunks.st: Rather, the entire deposit, i.e., both vessels,

chunks.en: until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: are placed in a safe place until Elijah comes or one of them admits his deceit.

summary: If someone left fruit with a watchman, the watchman may not touch it even if it is spoiling. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says he sells it in front of beis din, like returning a lost thing.

chunks.en: If someone leaves fruit with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits produce with another,

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ הֵן אֲבוּדִין לֹא יִגַּע בָּהֶן.
chunks.en: even if it is going to waste, he should not touch it.
chunks.explain: It is not his.
chunks.st: even if it is lost due to spoilage or vermin, the bailee may not touch it, as it is not his.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: he sells it in front of beis din,
chunks.st: He sells it before the court,

chunks.en: because it is like returning a lost thing to its owner.
chunks.st: as by doing so he is like one returning a lost item to the owner,
chunks.stMore: since through its sale he prevents the owner from losing the value of his produce.

summary: When a watchman gives back fruit, he may take off a set amount that fruit normally shrinks. The Sages argue about how much and for how big a pile.

chunks.en: If someone leaves fruit with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits produce with another, and the bailee provides him with different produce in return,

chunks.en: the watchman may take off the amount it shrinks.
chunks.explain: Stored fruit dries up and mice eat some.
chunks.st: that bailee deducts from the produce that he returns an amount equal to the standard decrease of the produce. The decrease is calculated according to this formula:

chunks.en: For wheat and rice,
chunks.st: For wheat and for rice,

chunks.en: nine half-kav for each kor.
chunks.explain: A kav and a kor are measures; a kor is 180 kav.
chunks.st: he deducts nine half-kav per kor, which is 180 kav;

chunks.en: For barley and millet,
chunks.st: for barley and millet,

chunks.en: nine kav for each kor.
chunks.st: he deducts nine kav per kor;

chunks.en: For spelt and flax seed,
chunks.st: for spelt and flaxseed,

chunks.en: three se'ah for each kor.
chunks.st: he deducts three se’a, which total eighteen kav, per kor.

chunks.en: It all goes by the amount,
chunks.st: The entire calculation is according to the measure,

chunks.en: it all goes by the time.
chunks.explain: This is the amount for one year.
chunks.st: and the entire calculation is according to the time
chunks.stMore: elapsed. This is the amount of produce that the bailee deducts per one kor of produce over the course of one year.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:

chunks.en: "Why should the mice care?
chunks.st: And what do the mice care how much produce the bailee is safeguarding?

chunks.he: וַהֲלֹא אוֹכְלוֹת בֵּין מֵהַרְבֵּה וּבֵין מִקִּמְעָא.
chunks.en: Don't they eat the same from a lot or from a little?
chunks.st: Don’t they eat the same amount whether it is from much produce and whether it is from little produce?

chunks.en: Rather, he takes off the shrinking
chunks.st: Rather, he deducts an amount equal to the standard decrease

chunks.en: only for one kor."
chunks.st: of just one kor of produce.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it was a big amount,
chunks.st: If the deposit was a large measure,

chunks.en: he does not take off anything,
chunks.st: the bailee does not deduct the decrease from it,

chunks.en: because it grows.
chunks.explain: Fruit can swell, so it evens out.
chunks.st: due to the fact that for different reasons it increases.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, he returns the measure of produce that was deposited with him, because the increase offsets the decrease.

summary: When giving back wine or oil, a watchman may take off a set amount for what soaks into the barrel and what sinks to the bottom. Rabbi Yehuda says a buyer of clear oil also accepts a set amount of sediment.

chunks.en: He may take off one sixth for wine.
chunks.explain: Wine soaks into the barrel and dries up.
chunks.st: When the bailee returns liquids that were deposited with him, he deducts one-sixth of the amount for wine,
chunks.stMore: to offset the decrease in volume due to absorption into the cask and evaporation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says, one fifth.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: He deducts one-fifth.

chunks.he: יוֹצִיא לוֹ שְׁלשֶׁת לֻגִּין שֶׁמֶן לְמֵאָה,
chunks.en: He takes off three lug of oil for each hundred:
chunks.explain: A lug is a small measure.
chunks.st: He deducts three log of oil for one hundred log:

chunks.en: a lug and a half for the dregs at the bottom,
chunks.st: A log and a half for sediment that sinks to the bottom of the cask,

chunks.en: and a lug and a half soaked into the barrel.
chunks.st: and a log and a half for absorption into the cask.

chunks.en: If it was clear, filtered oil,
chunks.st: If it was refined oil,

chunks.en: he does not take off for dregs.
chunks.st: he does not deduct any of the oil for sediment because it was filtered.

chunks.en: If the barrels were old,
chunks.st: If the oil was stored in old casks that are already saturated,

chunks.en: he does not take off for soaking in.
chunks.explain: Old barrels are already full of oil and soak up no more.
chunks.st: he does not deduct any of the oil for absorption.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even someone who sells filtered oil
chunks.st: Even in a case of one who sells refined oil

chunks.en: to his friend all year round,
chunks.st: to another all the days of the year,

chunks.en: the buyer accepts on himself
chunks.st: this buyer accepts upon himself that the seller will deduct

chunks.en: a lug and a half of dregs for each hundred.
chunks.st: a log and a half of sediment for one hundred log, as that is the standard measure of sediment.

summary: A watchman moved a barrel he was watching and it broke. Whether he pays depends on whether he moved it for himself or for the barrel, whether it broke in his hand, and whether the owner gave it a set place.

chunks.en: If someone left a barrel with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits a barrel with another,

chunks.en: and the owner did not set a place for it,
chunks.st: and the owners did not designate a specific place for the barrel to be stored in the bailee’s house,

chunks.en: and he moved it and it broke:
chunks.st: and the bailee moved it and it broke,

chunks.en: if it broke in his hand,
chunks.st: if it broke while still in his hand,

chunks.en: if he moved it for himself, he must pay;
chunks.st: there is a distinction: If he moved the barrel for his purposes, he is liable to pay for the damage.

chunks.en: if for the barrel's good, he is free.
chunks.st: If he moved the barrel for its own purposes, to prevent it from being damaged, he is exempt.

chunks.en: If it broke after he put it down,
chunks.st: If, after he replaced the barrel it broke,

chunks.en: whether for himself or for the barrel, he is free.
chunks.st: whether he initially moved it for his purposes or whether he moved it for its own purposes, he is exempt.

chunks.en: If the owner set a place for it,
chunks.st: But if the owners designated a specific place for the barrel,

chunks.en: and he moved it and it broke,
chunks.st: and the bailee moved it and it broke,

chunks.en: whether in his hand or after he put it down:
chunks.st: whether it broke while still in his hand or whether it broke after he replaced the barrel,

chunks.en: if for himself, he must pay;
chunks.st: if he moved it for his purposes he is liable to pay,

chunks.en: if for the barrel's good, he is free.
chunks.st: and if he moved it for its own purposes, he is exempt.

summary: A watchman who did not guard coins the way watchmen normally do must pay if they are lost. If he guarded them properly, he does not pay.

chunks.en: If someone left coins with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposited coins with another,

chunks.en: and he tied them up and hung them behind his back,
chunks.st: and that bailee bound it in a cloth and slung it behind him,

chunks.en: or gave them to his young son or daughter,
chunks.st: or conveyed them to his minor son or daughter for safeguarding,

chunks.en: or locked the door in front of them in a bad way,
chunks.st: or locked the door before them in an inappropriate, i.e., insufficient, manner to secure them,

chunks.en: he must pay, because he did not guard the way watchmen guard.
chunks.st: the bailee is liable to pay for the coins, as he did not safeguard the coins in the manner typical of bailees.

chunks.en: But if he guarded the way watchmen guard, he is free.
chunks.st: But if he safeguarded the money in the manner that bailees safeguard items and it was nevertheless stolen, he is exempt.

summary: If money left with a money changer is tied up, he may not use it; if it is loose, he may, and then he must pay if it is lost. A regular person may never use it; the Tannaim argue about a storekeeper.

chunks.en: If someone leaves coins with a money changer,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits money with a money changer,

chunks.en: if they are tied up,
chunks.st: if the money is bound,

chunks.en: he may not use them,
chunks.st: the money changer may not use it.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן,
chunks.en: so if they get lost, he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: Therefore, if it is lost he does not bear responsibility for it.

chunks.en: If they are loose, he may use them,
chunks.explain: The owner knows a money changer uses coins.
chunks.st: If the money was unbound, the money changer may use it.

chunks.en: so if they get lost, he must pay.
chunks.st: Therefore, if it is lost he bears responsibility for it.

chunks.en: If they were left with a regular person,
chunks.st: If he deposited money with a homeowner,

chunks.en: whether tied up or loose,
chunks.st: whether it is bound or whether it is unbound,

chunks.en: he may not use them,
chunks.st: the homeowner may not use it,
chunks.stMore: as it never entered the mind of the depositor that the homeowner might use the money.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן.
chunks.en: so if they get lost, he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: Therefore, if the homeowner lost the money, he does not bear responsibility for it.

chunks.en: A storekeeper is like a regular person.
chunks.st: If the bailee is a storekeeper, his status is like that of a homeowner;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: a storekeeper is like a money changer.
chunks.st: If the bailee is a storekeeper, his status is like that of a money changer.

summary: A watchman who used a deposit for himself must pay for it, and the Tannaim argue about which value he pays. Only really using it makes him responsible, and lifting a barrel counts as taking all of it.

chunks.en: If a watchman uses a deposit for himself,
chunks.explain: He takes what he is watching for his own use.
chunks.st: With regard to one who misappropriates a deposit,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he loses out whether its value went down or up.
chunks.explain: He pays whichever value is higher.
chunks.st: He is penalized for its decrease and its increase.
chunks.stMore: If the value of the deposit decreases, the bailee is liable to pay in accordance with its value at the time of the misappropriation. If it increases in value, he is liable to pay in accordance with its value at the time of repayment.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he took it.
chunks.st: He pays in accordance with its value at the time of removal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: what it was worth when the owner asks for it.
chunks.st: He pays in accordance with its value at the time of the claim.

chunks.en: If someone plans to use a deposit for himself,
chunks.st: With regard to one who intends to misappropriate a deposit and voices that intent in the presence of witnesses,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say he must pay.
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: He is liable to pay for any damage to the deposit from that point forward,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁלַח בּוֹ יָד,
chunks.en: he does not pay until he really uses it,
chunks.st: He is liable to pay only if he actually misappropriates the deposit,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated concerning a bailee:

chunks.he: אִם לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵהוּ.
chunks.en: "if he did not put his hand on his friend's things."
chunks.st: “Whether he has misappropriated his neighbor’s goods” (Exodus 22:7).

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. הִטָּה אֶת הֶחָבִית וְנָטַל הֵימֶנָּה רְבִיעִית,
chunks.en: How so? If he tipped the barrel and took a revi'is from it,
chunks.explain: A revi'is is a small cup of wine.
chunks.st: If he tilted the deposited barrel and took from it a quarter-log of wine for his own use,

chunks.en: and it broke, he pays only for the revi'is.
chunks.st: and the barrel broke, then he pays only for that quarter-log.

chunks.en: If he lifted it and took a revi'is from it,
chunks.st: If he lifted the barrel and took from it a quarter-log of wine,

chunks.en: and it broke, he pays for all of it.
chunks.explain: Lifting it made it his.
chunks.st: and the barrel broke, since he acquired the barrel by lifting it, he pays the value of the entire barrel.
